a-modern-cinderella-or-the-little-old-sh.title: A Modern Cinderella; Or, The Little Old Shoe, and Other Stories
a-modern-cinderella-or-the-little-old-sh.creator: Louisa May Alcott

arxiv-1610-01291.title: Word2Vec vs DBnary: Augmenting METEOR using Vector Representations or Lexical Resources?
arxiv-1610-01291.creator: Christophe Servan, Alexandre Bérard, Zied Elloumi, Hervé Blanchon & Laurent Besacier
arxiv-1610-01291.description: Abstract This paper presents an approach combining lexico-semantic resources and distributed representations of words applied to the evaluation in machine translation (MT). This study is made through the enrichment of a well-known MT evaluation metric: METEOR. This metric enables an approximate match (synonymy or morphological similarity) between an automatic and a reference translation.

arxiv-2108-08190.title: Higher-order interactions can better optimize network synchronization
arxiv-2108-08190.creator: Per Sebastian Skardal, Lluís Arola-Fernández, Dane Taylor, Alex Arenas
arxiv-2108-08190.description: Abstract Collective behavior plays a key role in the function of a wide range of physical, biological, and neurological systems where empirical evidence has recently uncovered the prevalence of higher-order interactions, i.e., structures that represent interactions between more than just two individual units, in complex network structures.

arxiv-2201-04930.title: Reduction Theorems for generalised block fusion systems
arxiv-2201-04930.creator: Patrick Serwene
arxiv-2201-04930.description: Abstract . We generalise Brauer’s Third Main Theorem, the First and Second Fong Reduction to generalised block fusion systems and apply the Second Fong Reduction to extend a result by Cabanes about the non-exoticity of fusion systems of unipotent blocks for finite groups of Lie type. 1.

arxiv-2207-00420.title: Cactus Mechanisms: Optimal Differential Privacy Mechanisms in the Large-Composition Regime
arxiv-2207-00420.creator: Wael Alghamdi, Shahab Asoodeh, Flavio P. Calmon, Oliver Kosut, Lalitha Sankar, Fei Wei
arxiv-2207-00420.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Wael Alghamdi, Shahab Asoodeh, Flavio P. Calmon, Oliver Kosut, Lalitha Sankar, Fei Wei. Most differential privacy mechanisms are applied (i.e., composed) numerous times on sensitive data. We study the design of optimal differential privacy mechanisms in the limit of a large number of compositions. As a consequence of the law of large numbers, in this regime the best privacy mechanism is the one that minimizes the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the conditional output distributions of the mechanism given two different inputs.

arxiv-2303-06030.title: Semiclassical transport in two-dimensional Dirac materials with spatially variable tilt
arxiv-2303-06030.creator: Abolfath Hosseinzadeh, S. A. Jafari
arxiv-2303-06030.description: Abstract We use Boltzmann theory to study the semi-classical dynamics of electrons in a two-dimensional (2D) tilted Dirac material in which the tilt varies in space. The spatial variation of the tilt parameter induces a non-trivial spacetime geometry on the background of which the electrons roam about.

arxiv-2310-16747.title: Spectral Background-Subtracted Activity Maps Journal: Research Notes of the AAS Facilities: SST – Swedish Solar Telescope, CHROMIS – Chromospheric Imaging Spectrometer BaSAMs ( Denker & Verma 2019 ) – MOMFBD ( van Noort et al. 2005 ) – CRISPRED ( de la Cruz Rodríguez et al. 2015 ) – SSTRED ( Löfdahl
arxiv-2310-16747.creator: Carsten Denker, Meetu Verma, Alexander G.M. Pietrow, Ioannis Kontogiannis, Robert Kamlah
arxiv-2310-16747.description: Abstract High-resolution solar spectroscopy provides a wealth of information from photospheric and chromospheric spectral lines. However, the volume of data easily exceeds hundreds of millions of spectra on a single observation day. Therefore, methods are needed to identify spectral signatures of interest in multidimensional datasets.

arxiv-2406-01239.title: Tighter yet more tractable relaxations and nontrivial instance generation for sparse standard quadratic optimization
arxiv-2406-01239.creator: Immanuel Bomze, Bo Peng, Yuzhou Qiu, E. Alper Yıldırım
arxiv-2406-01239.description: Abstract The Standard Quadratic optimization Problem (StQP), arguably the simplest among all classes of NP-hard optimization problems, consists of extremizing a quadratic form (the simplest nonlinear polynomial) over the standard simplex (the simplest polytope/compact feasible set). As a problem class, StQPs may be nonconvex with an exponential number of inefficient local solutions.

arxiv-2502-00084.title: A uniform rate of convergence for the entropic potentials in the quadratic Euclidean setting
arxiv-2502-00084.creator: Pablo López-Rivera
arxiv-2502-00084.description: Abstract . We bound the rate of uniform convergence in compact sets for both entropic potentials and their gradients towards the Brenier potential and its gradient, respectively. Both results hold in the quadratic Euclidean setting for absolutely continuous measures satisfying some convexity assumptions. 1. Introduction 1.1.

arxiv-2503-23983.title: Quantum computing within a bosonic context: Assessing finite basis effects on prototypical vibrational Hamiltonian spectra
arxiv-2503-23983.creator: Joachim Knapik, Bruno Senjean, Benjamin Lasorne, Yohann Scribano
arxiv-2503-23983.description: Abstract Quantum computing has recently been emerging in theoretical chemistry as a realistic avenue meant to offer computational speedup to challenging eigenproblems in the context of strongly-correlated molecular systems or extended materials. Most studies so far have been devoted to the quantum treatment of electronic structure, for which the transformation of fermionic operators into the qubit space is quite transparent.

arxiv-2507-03170.title: ASCRIBE-XR: Virtual Reality for Visualization of Scientific Imagery
arxiv-2507-03170.creator: Ronald J. Pandolfi \IUCrCemaillink ronpandolfi@lbl.gov \IUCrOrcidlink 0000-0003-0824-8548, Jeffrey J. Donatelli \IUCrCemaillink jjdonatelli@lbl.gov \IUCrOrcidlink 0009-0003-7173-0174, Julian Todd \IUCrEmaillink julian@goatchurch.org.uk, Daniela Ushizima \IUCrEmaillink dushizima@lbl.gov \IUCrOrcidlin
arxiv-2507-03170.description: Abstract ASCRIBE-XR, a novel computational platform designed to facilitate the visualization and exploration of 3D volumetric data and mesh data in the context of synchrotron experiments, is described. Using Godot and PC-VR technologies, the platform enables users to dynamically load and manipulate 3D data sets to gain deeper insights into their research.

arxiv-2508-20112.title: Should one (be allowed to) replace the Cippolini’s?
arxiv-2508-20112.description: Abstract One examines and discusses proposals on whether riders could be replaced in a team during multi-stage races, and how much a team final time at the end of the race would change (be ”adjusted”) if only the riders having completed the race are taken into account for ranking teams.

arxiv-2511-07218.title: The Long Shadow of Superstars: Effects on Opportunities, Careers, and Team Production Thanks: I am grateful to Ryo Nakajima for his valuable comments and suggestions that greatly improved this paper. I thank Reio Tanji, a baseball analyst, for sharing his domain expertise and providing insightful fe
arxiv-2511-07218.creator: Masaya Nishihata
arxiv-2511-07218.description: Abstract Superstars often dominate key tasks because of their exceptional abilities, but this concentration of responsibility may unintentionally limit on-the-job learning opportunities for others. Using panel data from Major League Baseball (MLB), this study examines how superstar presence affects teammates’ opportunities and career outcomes.

arxiv-2602-22735.title: Simulation-based Optimization for Augmented Reading
arxiv-2602-22735.creator: Yunpeng Bai, Shengdong Zhao, Antti Oulasvirta
arxiv-2602-22735.description: Abstract . Augmented reading systems aim to adapt text presentation to improve comprehension and task performance, yet existing approaches rely heavily on heuristics, opaque data-driven models, or repeated human involvement in the design loop. We propose framing augmented reading as a simulation-based optimization problem grounded in resource-rational models of human reading.

pmc-10542330.creator: Ke Qiu, Xing Duan, Minzi Mao, Yao Song, Yufang Rao, Danni Cheng, Lan Feng, Xiuli Shao, Chuanhuan Jiang, Hai Huang, Yan Wang, Huifang Li, Xuemei Chen, Sisi Wu, Dan Luo, Fei Chen, Xingchen Peng, Yongbo Zheng, Haiyang Wang, Jun Liu, Yu Zhao, Xiangrong Song, Jianjun Ren
pmc-10542330.description: Although mRNA vaccines are known as potent activators of antigen-specific immune responses against infectious diseases, limited understanding of how they drive the functional commitment of CD8+ T cells in tumor microenvironment (TME) and secondary lymphoid organs hinders their broader application in cancer immunotherapy.

pmc-11476300.title: Measurable Residual Disease Testing in Multiple Myeloma Following T-Cell Redirecting Therapies
pmc-11476300.creator: Kevin Guanwen Shim, Rafael Fonseca
pmc-11476300.description: Simple SummaryMultiple myeloma (MM) is a blood cancer which classically has a prolonged course of remissions and relapses. Several new highly efficacious medications have been developed for MM in recent years, including some that utilize the body’s own immune cells to control the cancer.

pmc-11638465.title: Underwater detection and clipping using a reopenable clip with a long hood for colonic diverticular bleeding
pmc-11638465.creator: Kazuya Miyaguchi, Yoshikazu Tsuzuki, Hiroyuki Imaeda
pmc-11638465.description: Short abstract Watch a video of this article. BRIEF EXPLANATION There are multiple treatments available for diverticular hemorrhage. 1 Endoscopic identification of stigmata of recent hemorrhage (SRH), especially visible vessels, is important but often difficult. 2 Exposed vessels are identified by aspirating the diverticulum with a long transparent hood and inverting it.

pmc-13074043.title: Increased Agmatine Degradation in Children with Specific Learning Disorder
pmc-13074043.creator: Serkan Kapancık, Elif Abanoz, Serap Çetinkaya, Ahmet Ozan Kaleci
pmc-13074043.description: Specific Learning Disability (SLD) describes persistent difficulties in academic skills in reading, writing, and mathematics, despite having normal intelligence. The exact origin of SLD is unknown. However, it is thought that biological factors and environmental conditions, along with genetic factors, contribute to the development of SLD. Agmatine, a neurotransmitter in the brain, plays a role in various biological processes.

pmc-13257716.title: Vitamin D Receptor–Macrophage–IL-23 Axis in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: Pathogenic Mechanisms and Therapeutic Hope
pmc-13257716.creator: Alexandra Grigoraș, Larisa Ghemiș, Ancuta Goriuc, Alice Murariu, Naomi Fiterman, Nura Jdid, Teofil Blaga, Georgeta Liliana Foia
pmc-13257716.description: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), including Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis, is characterized by chronic intestinal inflammation driven by dysregulated immune responses in gut microbiota. Interleukin (IL)-23, a member of IL-12 cytokine family, has emerged as a key immune mediator, being produced mainly by macrophages from the intestinal mucosa.

pmc-13381819.title: Non-contact alcohol detection in mice using an imaging photoplethysmography (IPPG) system
pmc-13381819.creator: Jea Young Choi, Kanghae Kim, Joo Beom Eom
pmc-13381819.description: We report on a method to determine whether alcohol has been consumed using camera-based, non-contact imaging photoplethysmography (IPPG) technology. IPPG signals were collected using a visible-band CMOS camera and a 520 nm light-emitting diode (LED). The light source was set to a uniform light output of 2.8 mW/cm², and images were captured at 150 frames per second.

pmc-13684561.title: Evidence for long-standing mild-effect mutator alleles shaping genetic variation in S. cerevisiae populations
pmc-13684561.creator: Pengyao Jiang, Vidha Sudhesh, Megan My-Ngan Phan, Ishan Bansal, Cian Wheeler, Alan J Herr, Maitreya J. Dunham, Kelley Harris
pmc-13684561.description: Most mutations are neutral or deleterious, and mutator alleles that substantially increase the mutation rate of an organism are believed to be short-lived in natural populations. Theory suggests that mutator alleles of modest effect have the potential to segregate nearly neutrally, but this prediction has been difficult to test experimentally.
